After finishing all 3 games on max dificulty, for me this is the best game in the modern Shadorwun trilogy. It took everything that made the previous games good and made it better. If you enjoyed previous entries or like CRPGs in general, you should give this one a try.

- Story / Dialogue: By far the best part of the game. Story is Interesting from the start, with a better pacing than in previous games. Companions also have a lot of personality and their personal quests are interesting. Dialogue is top-notch. There is also more 'party banter' based on which companions you pick for each mission and your decisions during these missions. Only downside is that it does not have voice acting at all, same as previous entries.

- Combat: Better audio-visual feedback and more options for you in combat. I still think that Shadowrun combat is its weakest link though. As an upside, here you can skip most of it with skill checks if you want. Bosses are also the best in the series.

- Progression: Has been expanded. You have access to new spells and items for any build you want to run. Cyberware has also been improved, and now you can create a full-on cyberpsycho with cyberware exclusive weapons (very fun build, shredding everything on your path).

- Decking: The system has seen some big changes and it does feel more dynamic than previous entries, but can still be a pain in the ass.

- Music: Music is amazing as always. Shadowrun doesn't miss in this department.

- Visuals: Personally I really like the visuals of Shadowrun and here the visuals are crispier than previous entries but are otherwise similar, giving you those vibes of being in a cyberpunk dystopia.

That said, 12.5hrs into my first run and...I'm going to have to start again. Without any sort of guidance or tutorial at the start (the tutorial is a laughably tiny booklet accessed through the menu) I automatically started playing the simplest character I could - Big Ork Go Bonk. 

Big Ork Go Bonk does not have any charisma. Big Ork Go Bonk does not understand the Matrix and avoids hacking at all costs. 

Big Ork Go Bonk has a big problem in the final missions when Charisma AND Hacking are mandatory to not be utterly destroyed. 

By this point, I vaguely understand how the gameplay works (outside of the Matrix) and am just crushed that I'll need to revert to a previous save or start again entirely to build a character that can actually progress.

3,5/5 Shadowrun: Hong Kong jatkaa Harebrained schemesin Shadowrun pelien sarjaa. Tällä kertaa seikkailu suuntaa nimensä mukaisesti Hong Kongiin, jossa pelaajahahmo päätyy keskelle salajuonta ja päätyy selvittämään isähahmonsa katoamista. Matkan alkupuolella päädytään paikallisen rikollispomon leipiin ja tästä oikeastaan lähdetään liikkeelle.

Verrattuna Shadowrun Returnsiin juoni ja mukaan liittyvät sivuhahmot ovat mielestäni selkeästi paremmin kirjoitettuja. Toisen positiivisen maininnan ansaitsee sivutehtävien määrä, laatu ja vaihtelevuus. Osassa tehtävissä mennään humoristisemmalla otteella ja osallistutaan hakkerien messuille tai kohdataan uuteen elämäntapaansa totutteleva vampyyri, osassa pääosassa on puhdas räiskintä ja osassa varteenotettavaksi vaihtoehdoksi muodostuu taistelujen välttely hiiviskelemällä, muutamia mainitakseni.

Hahmoluokat ja niiden kautta tarjolla oleva vaihtelu, taistelut ja niiden varovaista suojasta suojaan etenemistä suosiva painotus, yläviistosta kuvattu grafiikka ja äänimaailma ovat pääosin aiemmista osista tuttuja. Tekstiä on tuttuun tapaan edelleen paljon, mutta se tuntuu jotenkin laadukkaammalta. Oikeastaan ainoa suurempi ärsytyksen aihe olivat muutamissa tehtävissä painottuvan hakkeroinnin määrä – hakkerointi jää tylsäksi ja itseään toistavaksi pakkopullaksi.

Kokonaisuutena suuria uudistuksia aikaisempiin osiin ei oikein tunnu olevan, mutta se mitä on tehty, on tehty riittävän hyvin ja Shadowrun: Hong Kong ansaitseekin varovaisen suosituksen. Erityisesti pelisarjan aiempiin osiin tykästyneiden kannattaa toki tämäkin katsastaa. Läpipeluukerrasta on vaikea antaa tarkkaa arviota. Kaikki sivutehtävät ja niiden eri variaatiot kahlaamalla läpipeluuseen kului noin 50 tuntia, mutta sivutehtäviä skippaamalla aikakin on todennäköisesti nipsaistavissa noin puoleen.

Having played the previous two I can say this one spoke to me the most. It streamlines and optimizes a lot of the jank from Returns and Dragonfall, and the art has improved a lot too, especially if you compare it to Returns. The music is also on par with Dragonfall, if not a little stronger in parts. The encounters do feel reasonably challenging on normal. I got through it reasonably well but still had to use my brain in some of the more tense encounters later on.

It's still a bit more light on the mechanics compared to other CRPGs like the ones from Owlcat or Larian, but where it really shines is its writing, especially when it comes to its characters. Every single one of your crewmembers and associates has something interesting going on. This extends even to the player character, since they have a predefined past which they can process in their own way. The main and sidequests really help flesh out its setting, mixing real life history with fiction. Between sabotaging a megacorp with feng shui, investigating murders around a zombie samurai for technopriests inside an abandoned shopping mall and befriending a B-Movie directors vampire secretary there's a lot of really unique sidequests to go through.

Where it falters a bit is the strength of its main story. The mystery about Raymond and Kowloon Walled City is still really well written but just not as tightly paced as taking up Monika Schäfers legacy in Dragonfall. Also while the writing can be good, it can go overboard a bit with some of the side characters.

Also while it finishes some loose threads, I don't really care for the extra content added by the definitive edition. There's still some great stories and characters in there but overall I just think it's just not as polished and ends on kind of a sour note with a binary decision that just doesn't quite feel earned.

Mechanically there are still some issues grandfathered in from the other games as well as some new ones. I appreciate the attempt of the devs to make hacking a little more involved, but playing simon says to break code was maybe not the best call. Luckily hacking is for the most part optional. 

But yeah, overall I still had a great time with it and wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone who likes mechanically lighter but well written CRPGs.

[h1]TL;DR[/h1]
This is masterpiece. The story, writing and world building are on an incredible level. Shadowrun: Hong Kong has been improved over Shadowrun: Dragonfall in every single aspect. Therefore I recommend to [b]play the Shadowrun series backwards[/b].
Story takes place in a really well designed dystopian world. The story, writing and world building have been improved to an incredible extend, are insanely good and they are easily the best part of the game. While The combat has, yet again, been improved it remains the weak point of Shadowrun, thanks to the clunky UI and missing keybinding options.

--------------------------------
[h1]Pros:[/h1]
[h2]Overall look and feel[/h2]
[list]
[*] The game looks even better than Dragonfall. Visuals are fantastic, even most of the character portraits are straight up beautiful.
[*] Music is good
[/list]

[h2]Gameplay[/h2]
[list]
[*] You don't gain XP from fights but by solving quests. This way there are no negative effects if you solve a quest diplomatically instead
[*] Alt key reveals objects you can interact with
[*] UI is way more useful, than it was in the Dragonfall which improved the combat, yet again, by a lot
[*] Even better map design to provide more tactical depth
[*] More variety in classes is available and each of them does play fairly unique
[*] Companions can be upgraded (interface is in a weird spot though)
[*] More variety in items and combat trees
[*] Not as much of an RNG hell as Dragonfall or Returns
[/list]

[h2]Story and world building[/h2]
[list]
[*] The world is interesting and contains a nice amount of visual detail
[*] Story is great
[*] World building is outstanding
[*] The writing is phenomenal
[*] Decisions have an impact
[*] There is much more story and world building than in Dragonfall, which are the strong suites of the Shadowrun series
[*] Multiple optional side missions, that you may or may not see depending on your choices and actions
[*] Extended Edition/DLC rounds up the story
[/list]

[h2]QoL[/h2]
[list]
[*] Mod support. Mods exist that add new stories to the game
[/list]



--------------------------------
[h1]Cons:[/h1]
[h2]Gameplay[/h2]
[list]
[*] Combat: Interface
[list]
        [*] Still by far my biggest gripe with the game, while it has been improved again, the combat interface could be improved further
        [*] Abilities can't be selected via keys, but only via mouse
        [*] No option to rebind any keys (I think)
        [*] Status effects are visible longer than they are applied. A burn dot will remain visible, even when there won't be another tick of damage, so it misleads your damage calculations for no reason at all
[/list]
[*] The location for the companion upgrades remains in a weird spot. I did not find the interface to upgrade my companions after the tutorial (just like for Dragonfall I forgot about it and it's placed in a weird location). Therefore I only found it near the end of my playthrough
[*] Grenade usage is still very situational. They require 2 AP and in most cases you are better of doing two different actions instead
[*] Inventory management is still fairly bad, but luckily you don't have to use it much
[*] In certain sections of the matrix precise movement are a requirement but if you click out of bounds or on terrain your decker won't register the input
[/list]

[h2]Bugs + missing QoL[/h2]
[list]
[*] Very limited set of options
[*] No borderless windowed mode
[*] Not all keybinds are shown in the menu
[*] Interactions like save require multiple clicks
[*] No autosave feature during the battle
[*] The quickload is not a quickload, but all it does is to open the load interface
[*] Loading times are still an eternity (the longer the game runs, the worse it gets)
[*] No music during those endless loading screens
[*] Picking up items mid mission can only be added to either your personal inventory or the stash in your home, not to any of your companions (including your team members). Finding new weapons or equipment basically does diddly ♥♥♥♥ for the current mission
[/list]

It's just not got nothing to really lift elevate it to a wortwhile experience. The combat system is functional, but not remotely exciting, and is best skipped completely, the hacking minigame got improved - but not in a way that wouldn't have made it being completely removed a much better improvement. So, the only thing that is left to carry it is the story, and unfortunately this one doesn't live to the premise.

It is interesting and alternative, dialogues are still intelligent, but the pacing is bad. What is more, the depth is superficial - there is the usual thorough escalation at the end, but even then, it is a mostly surface level experience. Sure, it's a glossy surface, but I still found like it was an RPG experience where I lacked the ability to make nuanced choices. The game bets a lot on trying to make itself more immersive for the player by adding him into the story with an introduction of an adoptive parent and father, but that didn't have me half as immersed as I was in Dragonfall with an empty backstory and the feeling that I actually affected circumstances around me. Basically, for an RPG to be good, I want to actually get to feel like I am shaping the story, not to be told how the story is about me without really feeling it, you know? 

It's made worse by the -awful- DLC. It feels like cut content, but is intended to wrap up the story. In the main story, the ending had a flatter feeling ending than Shadowrun Returns - and SH Returns was almost a tech demo, so imagine how poor of an experience it felt. But the DLC completely failed on that regard, giving us the ultimate choice with zero nuance, and overall actually managing to make the overall taste of the experience even worse. 

Ultimately, Dragonfall was the best this series got, and if you are wondering which of the three to buy, only buy that one.

Однако если ты сам не декер, а на эту роль берёшь Из0бель в свою пати, то не можешь выбрать набор программ, с которыми она пойдет в Матрицу (киберпространство).

Единственный плюс игры декером - весьма жирные плюшки за успешный взлом.

- Если любишь пылесосить локации и таскать кучу лута, то забудь. Каждый раз, когда можно что-то поднять и положить в инвентарь, тут ощущается как маленький праздник.

- С лутанием денег та же история. Изредка можешь подобрать, но большую их часть дают за выполнение контрактов. Кому-то норм, мне же на средней сложности приходилось постоянно выкручиваться и экономить на грани духоты.

- Нельзя самому распределять поинты на своих сопартейцах. Их прокачка упрощена до (икскома) 6 уровней, на каждом из которых ты выбираешь один из двух перков плюс небольшая пассивная прибавка к статам. И да, я не зря вспомнил про икском - в здешних боях тоже частенько возможны бесячие промахи. 

- Так как не можешь сам распределять поинты на сопартийцах, то в лейте не все из них смогут пользоваться топовыми пушками. 

- ППшки и вовсе показались мне бесполезным мусором, а не оружием (Даже когда Гоббет докачалась до своего максимума, она все равно скорее попадёт в своего, чем во врага. Либо попадёт, но урон зачастую мизерный)

Вместо "залоченной" пушки или одежды можно поставить свою, на в каждой миссии это будет сбрасываться.
Нужная экипировка сохраняется только на твоём персонаже.

Hot take perhaps, but I think this game is peak Shadowrun and yes, by that I mean that I prefer Hong Kong to Dragonfall in almost every aspect, except decking.

This game is saturated to the brim with Shadowrun's atmosphere, from the music, to the NPCs, to the companions, enemies and locations. Everything (except decking, that got a bit worse) has been improved: cybernetic augments, magic, build variety, combat, weapons, systems, fluidity and missions.

I'm normally not a fan of oriental settings, but this game just clicked. I struggle to pinpoint exactly what it is that makes the game so appealing, but if I had to guess it has to be probably the social dynamics between some great characters, my favourite of which is Kindly Chen. The whole Shadowrunner side of things was a bit wishy-washy in Dragonfall in the sense that it was a very generic and "in the background" thing, whereas in Hong Kong you actually feel part of the criminal underworld: a cold, brutal and unforgiving place where, after a time, you'll eventually fit in. It's so satisfying to see how you get gradually acknowledged by the people around you, gaining both respect and admiration. The focus is more on you in this game rather than an opaque mystery that plays like a detective's movie, which makes you feel more involved in the story at a personal level, especially through the character of Duncan.

To this day, at times, I think about Shadowrun: Hong Kong, once in a while, and end up googling if there is, perhaps, any news about a new title in the making. Shadworun has great potential, especially now that cprgs are a bit less niche. Hopefully someone will pick up the torch and give us something new without compromising the complexity and articulate nature of this beautiful setting.
